memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You are also directed to tell them, "Do this: Take some carts from Egypt for your children and your wives, and get your father and come. Never mind about your belongings, because the best of all Egypt will be yours."'" — Gen 45:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Never mind about your belongings." What a striking instruction. Do not spend energy dragging your old possessions across the desert — what is waiting for you is better than anything you would carry.

Jacob's family owned very little worth keeping. A few worn tents, some household items, whatever survives in a famine. Egypt's best was on offer, and holding onto the old would only slow them down.

We can be strangely attached to things that are not worth the carrying. Old comforts. Old ways of coping. Habits and identities that felt necessary once. God calls us forward, and we come dragging bags we should have left behind.

Paul described his impressive religious credentials — his pedigree, his zeal, his blameless record — and then called all of it rubbish compared to knowing Christ (Phil 3:7-8). Not because those things were shameful, but because what he had found was so much better.

The invitation here is not to despise what you have. It is to hold it loosely, because what God has for you is better. Whatever you are tempted to drag along, ask whether it is worth the weight when the best of everything is already promised to you in Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you carrying that God may be asking you to leave behind?
2. Do you hold your possessions loosely or tightly?
3. What is it costing you to hold onto something old?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me hold everything loosely and travel light. Show me what I am dragging along that I should have left behind, and let knowing Christ be worth more to me than all of it. Amen.
